<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta is a work on Sanskrit poetics that is considered as one of Ruyyaka's major works, along with the Alaṅkārasūtra. Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta is divided into two parts: the first part deals with the nature and types of poetry, while the second part deals with the theory and practice of composition.<br><br>In the first part of Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta, Ruyyaka discusses the definition of poetry and its various types, such as epic, drama, lyric, and didactic poetry. He also explains the concept of rasa, or aesthetic experience, and the various emotions or moods that can be conveyed through poetry. In addition, he discusses the importance of grammar and language in poetry, and how these elements can contribute to its aesthetic appeal.<br><br>The second part of Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta focuses on the practical aspects of poetry composition. Ruyyaka discusses the use of figures of speech (alaṅkāra) in poetry and how they can enhance its aesthetic appeal. He also provides guidelines for the use of different meters and styles of poetry, and offers advice on how to structure and organize a poem. Throughout the work, Ruyyaka emphasizes the importance of originality, creativity, and innovation in poetry composition.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta is a treatise on Sanskrit poetics, written by Rājānaka Ruyyaka in the 12th century. The work is divided into two parts, each dealing with different aspects of poetry and poetics.<br>The first part of the work deals with the nature and types of poetry. Ruyyaka begins by defining what poetry is and its various types, such as epic, drama, lyric, and didactic poetry. He then explains the concept of rasa, which is the aesthetic experience that is created by poetry, and the different emotions or moods that can be conveyed through poetry. Ruyyaka also discusses the importance of grammar and language in poetry, and how these elements can contribute to its aesthetic appeal.<br>The second part of Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta focuses on the theory and practice of composition. Ruyyaka discusses the use of figures of speech, or alaṅkāra, in poetry and how they can enhance its aesthetic appeal. He also provides guidelines for the use of different meters and styles of poetry, and offers advice on how to structure and organize a poem. Ruyyaka emphasizes the importance of originality, creativity, and innovation in poetry composition, and encourages poets to experiment with new forms and styles.<br>Throughout Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta, Ruyyaka draws upon earlier works of Sanskrit poetics, such as the Nāṭyaśāstra and the Alaṅkārasūtra, but also adds his own insights and ideas. The work is highly regarded for its comprehensive and detailed treatment of Sanskrit poetics, and is considered an important contribution to the field.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta is a unique work in Sanskrit poetics due to its comprehensive treatment of the subject matter. Unlike many earlier works on poetics, which focus primarily on the use of figures of speech, Ruyyaka's work covers a wide range of topics, including the nature and types of poetry, the concept of rasa, the importance of grammar and language, and guidelines for composition.<br>Another unique aspect of Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta is Ruyyaka's emphasis on the importance of originality and creativity in poetry composition. He encourages poets to experiment with new forms and styles, and to strive for unique and innovative expressions of their ideas and emotions.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature, particularly in the field of poetics. Ruyyaka's work is unique in its comprehensive treatment of the subject matter, which covers a wide range of topics, including the nature and types of poetry, the concept of rasa, the importance of grammar and language, and guidelines for composition. In addition, the emphasis on the importance of originality and creativity in poetry composition is a notable aspect of the work.<br><br>Kāvyaprakāśasaṅkēta of Rājānaka Ruyyaka is a comprehensive and influential work on poetics in Sanskrit literature. It is noted for its detailed and practical approach to the art of poetry, providing guidance on various aspects of poetic composition such as style, ornamentation, and the use of literary devices. The work also includes discussions on the different forms and genres of poetry, and is considered to be one of the most important treatises on Sanskrit poetics. Its impact can be seen in the works of many later poets and scholars, and it continues to be studied and appreciated by scholars of Indian literature today.</div></div></div>
